findings.title: Boolean conversion of PublishReceipt may not match intent
findings.body: The change replaces `receipt.accepted` with `bool(receipt)`, which relies on the truthiness of `PublishReceipt`. If `PublishReceipt` is a dataclass or object without a custom `__bool__` method, this will always evaluate to `True` (since non-empty objects are truthy), breaking the original logic that explicitly checked the `accepted` attribute. This violates the `Error Handling Standards` rule (1) by silently altering the intended behavior without explicit error handling or propagation.

findings.title: Naming inconsistency with custom rule
findings.body: The function `was_accepted` suggests it checks a boolean condition, but the new implementation `bool(receipt)` obscures the intent. The original `receipt.accepted` was explicit. This violates the `Naming Consistency` rule (1) by introducing a less descriptive name for the same concept.

summary.problem: The change to `was_accepted` breaks correctness by altering the logic and violates naming consistency rules.
summary.done_well: The function is concise and the diff is minimal.
